# /crav1-create-feature-branch

[All skills](../skills.md) · Walkthrough: [From a draft spec to an accepted spec](../../from-draft-spec.md) · Playbook: [`SKILL.md`](../../../.cursor/skills/crav1/crav1-create-feature-branch/SKILL.md)

## Purpose

Create or check out feat/<slug> (one branch for spec+build) or spec/<slug> (specify-only; build later on feat/<slug>).

Prompt for `feat/<slug>` or specify-only `spec/<slug>`; no silent checkout, no push, no PR.

1.64.0: the Build prompt puts a task's `(branch: …)` first, marked (Recommended), and never creates it from default without asking.

1.99.0: implementation code is never built on a base branch (main, master, develop, Merges into, `release/*`): no Stay there; Create `feat/<slug>` from the into branch (Recommended), Use an existing branch, Other name or Stop; `hotfix/` is a work prefix; specs, docs and the specs repo are exempt. Rules in `references/code-branch.md`.

1.68.0: a missing task sub-branch is offered as **Create it from the spec branch (Recommended)**; the `(into …)` marker is written after the yes.

1.129.0: a task's Build prompt offers the branch `scripts/build_map.py --recommend T#` prints, the same name as the build map row: `(map:)`, else `(branch:)`, else the plan step, else `committed later on`. The branch question is its own card, and a typed name on that card is the answer. A different pick writes `(map: <picked>)` on the task in the specs repo and does not commit it.

1.140.0: a branch named on the task line wins over the plan step. That is `(map:)`, else `(branch:)`, else a `feat/…` name in the sentence, else `committed later on`. `from <base>` after that name is the base, for example `feat/orders-host-setup-scripts from develop`. The plan step is the fallback when the task line names none. `--recommend` prints the branch on the first line, then `source: task line`, `source: build map`, or `source: new`, and `because:` when a merged or deleted branch was skipped. A merged pull request, a tip already in the base or the default branch, or a branch deleted locally and on the remote is not offered. The card lists the recommended option first. The description says where the name came from. When `because:` is present, that sentence is the description.

1.130.0: a typed branch name is that card's free-text answer, hint `Type a branch name`. There is no option labelled Other name.

## Runs when

Brownfield: leave the default branch. Called by the user, [`/crav1-spark-to-spec`](crav1-spark-to-spec.md), [`/crav1-ideas-to-spec`](crav1-ideas-to-spec.md), [`/crav1-bundle-to-specs`](crav1-bundle-to-specs.md), [`/crav1-existing-to-specs`](crav1-existing-to-specs.md), [`/crav1-build-tasks`](crav1-build-tasks.md), and [`/crav1-build-features`](crav1-build-features.md).

## Prompts

Prompt budget: 1 (the most prompts in one run, the closing yes included). A prompt may hold several questions. See the asking rule in `crav1.mdc`.

## Reads

In short: Current branch, default branch, dirty tree.

Reads the current branch, the default branch, and whether the tree is dirty.

## Writes

In short: A local `feat/<slug>` or `spec/<slug>` checkout.

Writes a local checkout of `feat/<slug>` or `spec/<slug>` after the user picks. When a build prompt picks a branch other than the build map's name for that task, writes `(map: <picked>)` on the task line in the specs repo and does not commit it.

## Does not

Leaves commits, push, and the pull request alone.

Limits and exceptions: skips the prompt when there is no repo, no commits, or the branch is already right. A dirty tree does not checkout.
